source.title: Memorizing Gaussians with no over-parameterizaion via gradient decent on neural networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Proves a memorization result for independently sampled Gaussian inputs in a specific depth-two network setting, extending the claim to a new synthetic input setting.
record.gate_note: Theorem 1 reports a one-step result on randomly labeled Gaussian examples. It does not report test error, so chance test error is not established. The paper also does not report fitting shuffled or independently permuted pixels, label-noise fractions, regularization comparisons, or learning patterns over training.
record.test_reason: Theorem 1 provides a theoretical test of random-label and Gaussian-input memorization using a depth-two network and one full gradient step. This addresses the fitting question by a different method from the original experiments.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: a single full gradient step from orthonormal initialization can memorize a near-optimal number of independently sampled, randomly labeled Gaussian examples using a depth-two network, under the stated assumptions.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies a depth-two network with orthonormal initialization on synthetic Gaussian examples, and proves a one-step gradient-descent result; it does not reproduce the original image experiments or their broader training setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The theorem is conditional on depth two, orthonormal initialization, the stated activation-function conditions, one gradient step, and the stated bounds on m and q.
record.problems: The result is a theorem for a restricted network and data distribution. It reports no test error, true-label comparison, or empirical replication; the authors list stochastic gradient descent, ReLU, non-Gaussian inputs, and other initialization schemes as open questions.

untested.parts: Chance test error, stochastic-gradient training, and fitting without changing architecture or hyperparameters relative to true-label training. The theorem covers a specific depth-two network, activation class, orthonormal initialization, and prescribed full-gradient step.
Relative training time for true and random labels, and convergence as label corruption increases.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and whether networks used for ordinary structured data also fit these inputs with unchanged training settings.
Intermediate corruption fractions, perfect fitting throughout a corruption sweep, and steady test-error degradation toward chance.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting, and true-label generalization after removing regularization.
Learning real patterns before noise and differences between real-label and random-label learning trajectories.

record.verdict_notes: The paper establishes complete fitting within its theoretical setting. It does not demonstrate failure outside that setting; the authors identify SGD, ReLU, non-Gaussian inputs, and other initializations as open extensions.

versions.untested_parts: Test error at chance and whether the same networks generalize well on true labels are not tested. The result is for a specific depth-two network, orthonormal initialization, and one full gradient step, not a general test of standard stochastic-gradient training or unchanged hyperparameters.
No comparison of training time for random versus true labels, or sweep over corrupted-label fractions.

The paper tests independently sampled Gaussian vectors with random labels, but not shuffled pixels or independently permuted pixels. It does not establish results for the same networks described in the claim.
No sweep from clean to fully corrupted labels, test-error measurements, or analysis of signal capture versus memorization.
No weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, or true-label generalization comparisons.
No training-time analysis of which patterns are learned first.

rows.subject: depth two network h_W
rows.size_stated: q hidden neurons; q ≥ log⁴(d); m ≤ log(d)q/log⁴(d)
rows.operation_detail: One gradient step on W from orthonormal initialization, using scaled hinge loss with step size η = m ln(d)/d.

conditions.value: O(1)-Lipschitz, piecewise twice differentiable with finitely many pieces and bounded second derivative; Eσ′(X)=0 for X∼N(0,1)

rows.measure: Training-set signed output margin yi hW+(xi), used by the paper's definition of memorization (yi h(xi)>0).
rows.value: For every i ∈ [m], yi hW+(xi) = Ω(ln(d)), with probability 1 − o(1).
rows.note: The theorem establishes positive training margins on random labels, hence memorization under the paper's stated definition. It does not report test error or a measured zero-error rate. Gaussian inputs overlap with V3's Gaussian-noise setting, but the study uses its own specific depth-two network and setup.
rows.check: Correct the sample-size bound to m ≤ dq/log⁴(d), rather than log(d)q/log⁴(d). Positive signed margins for every training example imply exactly zero training classification error with probability 1 − o(1); the fitting effect is therefore observed, not partial. The restricted setup and unmeasured test error are coverage limitations, not incomplete fitting.
